#Classification using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models

---


> Introduction
Machine Learning and Deep Learning are widely used techniques for solving real-world
classification problems. These models learn patterns from data and make predictions based
on input features.
In this project, we implement a complete classification pipeline using multiple Machine
Learning and Deep Learning algorithms. The goal is to analyze data, train different models,
and compare their performance to identify the best-performing approach.
This project also demonstrates the importance of data preprocessing, feature engineering,
and model evaluation in building an effective predictive system.

# We applied a Decision Tree Classifier to predict income levels.
# Decision Trees are prone to overfitting, so we controlled
# the model complexity using the `max_depth` parameter.

# We experimented with multiple depth values to find the best balance
# between bias and variance.
In [139]:
for depth in [3, 5, 7, 10]:
    model_dt = tree.DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=depth, random_state=42)
    model_dt.fit(X_train, y_train)

    print(f"Depth: {depth}")
    print("Train Accuracy:", model_dt.score(X_train, y_train))
    print("Test Accuracy :", model_dt.score(X_test, y_test))
    print("-"*40)
Depth: 3 Train Accuracy: 0.7988777400005528 Test Accuracy : 0.8015478164731896 ---------------------------------------- Depth: 5 Train Accuracy: 0.8264643281643033 Test Accuracy : 0.8286346047540077 ---------------------------------------- Depth: 7 Train Accuracy: 0.8303341902313625 Test Accuracy : 0.833167495854063 ---------------------------------------- Depth: 10 Train Accuracy: 0.8361942670757664 Test Accuracy : 0.8342730790491985 ----------------------------------------
In [140]:
# We evaluated multiple values of max_depth to control model complexity.
# As depth increased, both training and testing accuracy improved,
# indicating that the model was not overfitting within this range.

# The best performance was achieved at max_depth = 10, which provided
# the highest test accuracy while maintaining a small gap between
# training and testing scores. Therefore, max_depth = 10 was selected
# as the optimal value.

from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, classification_report, confusion_matrix
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Train SVM model
svm_model = SVC(kernel='rbf', random_state=42)

svm_model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predictions
y_pred_svm = svm_model.predict(X_test)

# Accuracy
svm_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred_svm)

print("SVM Accuracy:", svm_acc)

# Classification Report
print("\nClassification Report:\n")
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred_svm))

# Confusion Matrix
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred_svm)

plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues')
plt.title("SVM Confusion Matrix")
plt.xlabel("Predicted")
plt.ylabel("Actual")
plt.show()

import ipywidgets as widgets
from IPython.display import display, HTML, clear_output
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix, classification_report, accuracy_score

# ======================================
# PREDICTIONS
# ======================================

y_pred_lr = model_lr.predict(X_test)
y_pred_dt = model_dt.predict(X_test)
y_pred_rf = rf_model.predict(X_test)

# ======================================
# STORE MODELS
# ======================================

models = {
    "Logistic Regression": (model_lr, y_pred_lr),
    "Decision Tree": (model_dt, y_pred_dt),
    "Random Forest": (rf_model, y_pred_rf),
    "SVM": (svm_model, y_pred_svm),
    "Neural Network": (mlp_model, y_pred_mlp)
}

# ======================================
# CUSTOM TITLE
# ======================================

header = widgets.HTML(
    value="""
    <div style='
        background: linear-gradient(90deg,#4f46e5,#7c3aed);
        padding:20px;
        border-radius:15px;
        text-align:center;
        color:white;
        font-size:30px;
        font-weight:bold;
        box-shadow:0px 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.2);
    '>
    Machine Learning Classification Dashboard
    </div>
    <br>
    """
)
# ======================================
# DROPDOWN
# ======================================

model_dropdown = widgets.Dropdown(
    options=list(models.keys()),
    description='Choose Model:',
    style={'description_width': 'initial'},
    layout=widgets.Layout(width='350px', height='40px')
)

# ======================================
# BUTTON
# ======================================

show_button = widgets.Button(
    description='Show Analysis',
    button_style='success',
    layout=widgets.Layout(width='200px', height='45px')
)
# ======================================
# OUTPUT AREA
# ======================================

output = widgets.Output()

# ======================================
# BUTTON FUNCTION
# ======================================

def show_results(b):

    with output:
        clear_output(wait=True)

        selected_model = model_dropdown.value
        model, predictions = models[selected_model]

        acc = accuracy_score(y_test, predictions)

        # Accuracy Card
        display(HTML(f"""
        <div style='
            background:#f3f4f6;
            padding:20px;
            border-radius:15px;
            margin-top:10px;
            box-shadow:0px 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
        '>
            <h2 style='color:#4f46e5;'>📊 {selected_model}</h2>
            <h3>Accuracy: {acc:.4f}</h3>
        </div>
        """))

        # Classification Report
        print("Classification Report:")
        print(classification_report(y_test, predictions))

        # Confusion Matrix
        cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, predictions)

        plt.figure(figsize=(7,5))

        sns.heatmap(
            cm,
            annot=True,
            fmt='d',
            cmap='coolwarm',
            linewidths=1,
            linecolor='white'
        )

        plt.title(f'{selected_model} Confusion Matrix', fontsize=16)
        plt.xlabel('Predicted Labels')
        plt.ylabel('True Labels')

        plt.show()

# ======================================
# BUTTON EVENT
# ======================================

show_button.on_click(show_results)

# ======================================
# MODEL COMPARISON GRAPH
# ======================================

def compare_models():

    comparison_df = results.copy()

    plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))

    bars = plt.bar(
        comparison_df['Model'],
        comparison_df['Accuracy']
    )

    plt.title('Model Accuracy Comparison', fontsize=16)
    plt.ylabel('Accuracy')
    plt.ylim(0,1)

    for bar in bars:
        yval = bar.get_height()
        plt.text(
            bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2,
            yval + 0.01,
            f'{yval:.2f}',
            ha='center'
        )

    plt.xticks(rotation=10)
    plt.show()

# ======================================
# COMPARE BUTTON
# ======================================

compare_button = widgets.Button(
    description='Compare All Models',
    button_style='info',
    layout=widgets.Layout(width='220px', height='45px')
)

compare_output = widgets.Output()


def compare_click(b):
    with compare_output:
        clear_output(wait=True)
        compare_models()

compare_button.on_click(compare_click)
# ======================================
# LAYOUT
# ======================================

controls = widgets.HBox([
    model_dropdown,
    show_button,
    compare_button
])

# ======================================
# DISPLAY EVERYTHING
# ======================================

display(header)
display(controls)
display(output)
display(compare_output)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#                     PROJECT CONCLUSION
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# In this project, a complete end-to-end classification pipeline
# was developed using both traditional Machine Learning and
# Deep Learning techniques.

# The project began with Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA),
# where the dataset was explored, cleaned, and preprocessed.
# Missing values, feature relationships, distributions,
# and correlations were analyzed to better understand the data.

# Different preprocessing techniques such as encoding,
# feature scaling, and train-test splitting were applied
# to prepare the dataset for model training.

# Five different classification models were implemented
# and evaluated on the same dataset:
#
# 1. Logistic Regression
# 2. Decision Tree
# 3. Random Forest
# 4. Support Vector Machine (SVM)
# 5. Neural Network (MLP)

# Each model was evaluated using:
# - Accuracy Score
# - Classification Report
# - Confusion Matrix

# Based on the experimental results, Random Forest achieved
# the highest overall performance among all models.
# The ensemble learning approach of Random Forest helped
# improve prediction accuracy while reducing overfitting.

# Decision Tree also performed well and provided high
# interpretability, making it easier to understand how
# decisions were made within the model.

# Support Vector Machine (SVM) demonstrated strong performance
# in handling complex class boundaries and nonlinear patterns,
# although it required comparatively more computational time.

# The Neural Network model successfully captured complex
# relationships within the dataset and achieved competitive
# results, showing the effectiveness of Deep Learning for
# classification tasks.

# Logistic Regression showed lower performance compared
# to the other models. This indicates that the dataset
# may contain nonlinear relationships that are difficult
# for linear models to classify effectively.

# Additional analysis such as feature importance,
# model comparison visualizations, confusion matrices,
# and performance graphs provided deeper insights into
# model behavior and predictive capabilities.

# An interactive GUI dashboard was also developed in
# Jupyter Notebook to create a more user-friendly and
# visually appealing interface for viewing model results,
# comparisons, and evaluation metrics.

# Overall, this project demonstrated the importance of:
# - Data preprocessing
# - Feature analysis
# - Model comparison
# - Performance evaluation
# - Visualization techniques

# The project concludes that ensemble methods and
# nonlinear models performed better for this dataset,
# while simpler linear models may struggle with
# complex data patterns.

# Future improvements may include:
# - Hyperparameter tuning
# - Cross-validation
# - Advanced Deep Learning architectures
# - Larger datasets
# - Real-time deployment using Flask or Streamlit

# This project successfully highlights how Machine Learning
# and Deep Learning models can be applied to solve
# real-world classification problems effectively.
